# OTPKeep v0.1.0 — Your two-factor codes, one shortcut away

Released on `2026-10-25`.

> OTPKeep is a free, private authenticator for TOTP, HOTP and Steam codes that lives in your menu bar: a click, a
> shortcut or a few typed letters give you the code, and your accounts never leave your own devices.

## Summary

This is the first public release of OTPKeep. It runs on macOS and Linux, keeps your two-factor accounts encrypted on
your computer, and puts every code within reach — the menu bar panel, global shortcuts, a search panel that can type
the code for you, and a command line. There is no sign-up, no cloud and no telemetry; your devices sync directly
with each other, nearby, only when you ask.

## Who this release is for

You sign in with two-factor codes many times a day, on the computer in front of you, and you would rather keep
those accounts on your own machines than in someone else's cloud.

If you have ever:

- reached for your phone, unlocked it and scrolled for the right account while the login page timed out
- pasted a code that expired on the way, and waited thirty seconds for the next one
- kept two-factor accounts in an app you could not export from, or that wanted an account of its own
- set up a new computer and had to add every account again, one QR code at a time

then OTPKeep puts every code a click or a shortcut away on that computer, brings your accounts in from where they
are now, and moves them to your next computer directly, without a server in between.

## What you can do now

**Copy a code without looking for it.** Click the menu bar icon and click the account, or press `⌃⌥⌘1` … `⌃⌥⌘0`
for your first ten accounts from anywhere — the code is on the clipboard before the login page notices.

**Type it straight into the page.** Press `⌃⌥⌘Space`, type a few letters of the name and press `⇧Enter`: OTPKeep
types the code into the field you were in. Plain `Enter` copies it instead.

**Bring your accounts with you.** Paste links, drop or paste QR code images, or import a file; every import shows
the current codes first, so you can compare them with the website before anything is saved.

**Find the right account in a long list.** Search names, services, accounts, tags and notes — Chinese pinyin and
initials included — and keep the list tidy with pins, tags, drag-to-reorder and a 30-day trash.

**Keep two computers in step, privately.** Pair them once; later, open a sync window on one, enter its code on the
other, and allow it.

## What's new

### Codes at hand

- **Menu bar panel.** A compact list with a countdown ring per code and the next code in its last five seconds, so
  you never paste one that expires on the way. Translucent, with an opacity you choose.
- **Global shortcuts.** The first ten accounts get `⌃⌥⌘1` … `⌃⌥⌘0` on macOS, and any account can have its own
  combination. Shortcuts stay on the device they were set on and are never synced.
- **Search panel that types for you.** A Spotlight-style box opened from anywhere. Typing needs macOS Accessibility
  permission; without it, or on Wayland, the code is copied instead and the panel says so.
- **Counter-based (HOTP) accounts** show **Generate** instead of a code, because every code moves the counter on;
  OTPKeep never uses one up just because you looked.
- **Command line.** `otpkeep code github` prints a code; every vault command can answer in JSON.

### Adding and moving accounts

- **Forgiving links.** Spaces, lower case and a missing issuer are repaired. Microsoft and Oracle proprietary codes
  are recognised and explained rather than failing silently; they cannot be imported.
- **Export anywhere.** An encrypted OTPKeep backup, `otpauth://` links, Google Authenticator transfer QR codes or a
  GoldenPassport file. Every unencrypted format asks before it is written.
- **Steam Guard** codes, alongside TOTP and HOTP.

### Managing accounts

- **Main window.** Names, notes, tags, pins, order, code settings, per-account shortcuts, QR codes and edit history;
  several accounts can be tagged, exported or moved to the trash at once.
- **Browser management page.** Served on `127.0.0.1` only and opened with a one-time link: rename accounts, write
  notes, set shortcuts and copy codes on a full-size page.

### Sync between your devices

- **Pair once, sync when you ask.** A short window you open (one to five minutes), an eight-digit pairing code, a
  six-digit check code compared on both screens, and your approval on the other device every time.

### Look and feel

- **English and Simplified Chinese**, following the system or chosen on any page; light and dark themes.

## Privacy and security

- **Encrypted on your device.** Accounts are stored with XChaCha20-Poly1305; the key lives in the system keychain, or
  is derived from an optional master password with Argon2id.
- **No account, no server, no telemetry.** OTPKeep uses the network only for sync with your own devices nearby while
  a window is open, and for the management page on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Sync you can trust.** The Noise protocol between your devices' Ed25519 identities; the one-time code is checked
  with SPAKE2, so a recorded session cannot be guessed offline.
- **Careful with the clipboard.** Copied codes are kept out of clipboard history apps and cleared after 30 seconds
  (adjustable), only if the clipboard still holds that code.
- **Never reads what is not its own.** OTPKeep never opens keys, passwords or keychain items other than its own.

## Install

- Script (macOS and Linux, fully automatic): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/otpkeep/main/install.sh | sh`
- Homebrew (macOS): `brew install --cask weikxs/tap/otpkeep`, or `brew upgrade --cask otpkeep`
- A package below; check it against `checksums.txt`

| File | Platform |
|---|---|
| `otpkeep_0.1.0_darwin_universal.dmg` | macOS, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `otpkeep_0.1.0_linux_amd64.deb` / `_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `otpkeep_0.1.0_linux_amd64.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE (x86_64) |
| `otpkeep_0.1.0_linux_amd64.AppImage` / `_arm64.AppImage` | Any Linux with glibc (x86_64 / arm64) |

Then open OTPKeep — it appears in the menu bar (macOS) or the system tray (Linux) — and add your first account.

## Compatibility

- macOS 11 (Big Sur) or newer on Apple silicon and Intel.
- Linux with glibc on x86_64 and arm64: Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 38+ and their relatives; other
  distributions through the AppImage. Typing codes works on X11, not on Wayland.
- English and Simplified Chinese; other system languages show English.
- Windows, Android and iOS are planned.

## What's coming next

- Windows and Android.
- A signed and notarized macOS app.

## Notes

- The macOS app is not signed by Apple yet; Homebrew and the install script remove the quarantine flag. If you open
  the disk image by hand, choose **Open Anyway** in System Settings → Privacy & Security the first time. See
  [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/weikxs/otpkeep/blob/v0.1.0/SECURITY.md).
- OTPKeep is new: keep another copy of your accounts (an encrypted backup is one click) until you trust it.
